title: Reported Speech Quiz 4
description: Report commands and requests, and choose the right reporting verb and its pattern.
instructions: Reported Speech: Commands, requests and reporting verbs.
Use the standard rule: the reporting verb is in the past and the situation is over, unless a question says otherwise.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Report this: 'Close the door,' she told him.
options: She told him close the door.
She told him that he closed the door.
She told him to close the door.
She told him he to close the door.
questions.explanation: A command becomes told + person + to + verb. Watch out: the imperative has no subject, so you cannot add he.

questions.question: Report this: 'Don't be late,' he told us.
options: He told us not to be late.
He told us don't to be late.
He told us to don't be late.
He told us no to be late.
questions.explanation: A negative command is told + person + not to + verb. Watch out: don't does not stay in the report.

questions.question: 'Please help me,' she said to Tom. → She {{1}} Tom {{2}} help her.
questions.explanation: A request is asked + person + to + verb. Watch out: said cannot be followed by a person + to.

questions.question: 'I promise I'll call,' he said. → He {{1}} to call.
questions.explanation: Promise takes a to-infinitive directly. Watch out: said to call is not possible.

questions.question: 'She suggested me to go' is correct.
questions.explanation: Suggest takes -ing or a that-clause: She suggested going, or She suggested that I go. Watch out: suggest never takes person + to.

questions.question: Report this: 'Let's go to the beach,' he said.
options: He said us to go to the beach.
He suggested to go to the beach.
He suggested us going to the beach.
He suggested going to the beach.
questions.explanation: Let's becomes suggest + -ing. Watch out: suggested us going and suggested to go are both wrong.

questions.question: Choose the reporting verb that fits the words.

rows.given: 'Thank you for your help,' she said.
'You should see a doctor,' she said to him.
'Be careful! The floor is wet,' he said to us.
'Would you like to come to my party?' she said to us.

questions.explanation: Each direct sentence shows a function: thanking, apologising, advising, warning or inviting. Watch out: advised gives a suggestion, while warned shows danger.

questions.question: Match each pattern with an example.
questions.explanation: Each reporting verb has its own pattern. Watch out: advise needs a person before to, but promise does not.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The subject, the verb told, the person, then not to and the verb. Watch out: not comes before to.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He said me to wait outside.
He told me to wait outside.
He told that I wait outside.
He said to wait me outside.
questions.explanation: Tell takes a person and to: He told me to wait outside. Watch out: said me and told that do not fit a command.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: She warned me don't touch it.
She advised me to rest.
He suggested to stay home.
He denied breaking the vase.
They promised to come.
questions.explanation: Advise needs a person, promise takes to, and deny takes -ing. Watch out: suggested to stay and warned me don't keep the wrong pattern.

questions.question: Report this: 'Sit down,' the teacher told the boy.
accepted: The teacher told the boy to sit down.
The teacher told the boy to sit down
The teacher told him to sit down.
The teacher told him to sit down
questions.explanation: The command becomes told + person + to + verb. Watch out: the boy may become him.
